name: PA-16
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+11 partisan baseline)
Incumbent Mike Kelly seeking re-election with a large financial advantage
Challenger Justin Wagner's minimal fundraising ($67K vs $1.2M)

model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Kelly: an R+11 district, incumbency, and a roughly 18-to-1 fundraising edge, with markets pricing his chances above 90%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-driven estimate of a mid-teens Republican margin.
model.watch: A major shift in the national political environment or a surge of outside spending for Wagner could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Mike Kelly, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a northwestern Pennsylvania district that leans strongly Republican. His Democratic challenger, Justin Wagner, has raised only about $67,000 and had roughly $38,000 on hand, while Kelly has raised nearly $1.2 million and holds over $1.3 million in cash. No outside spending has been reported on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Kelly a win probability above 90 percent. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes Kelly a clear favorite, though not without any residual uncertainty given the absence of polling.
